parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the balancing of a metre rule. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Place the metre rule on the pivot at the 50.0 cm mark. • Place object P with its centre on the metre rule at the 10.0 cm mark.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record, in Table 1.1, the distance a from the centre of object P to the pivot. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) • Place object Q on the metre rule. • Keep object P at the 10.0 cm mark and adjust the position of object Q until the metre rule is as close to balancing as possible. Record, in Table 1.1, the distance b between the centre of object Q and the pivot. [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Repeat the steps above with object P placed at the 15.0 cm mark, 20.0 cm mark, 25.0 cm mark and 30.0 cm mark. Record all the values of a and b in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 a / cm b / cm [2]

ms.label: 1(a)(iii)
ms.text:
table: a values 35(.0), 30(.0), 25(.0), 20(.0) (cm)
b values decreasing and all table values to the nearest mm

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against b / cm ( x -axis). You do not need to start your graph from the origin (0,0). [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
axes correctly labelled with quantity AND unit AND the right way round
suitable scales
all plots correct to ½ small square
good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [3]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
triangle method clearly shown on graph
triangle covering at least ½ of candidate’s line between extreme plots
G = 1.8–2.2 inclusive
